summary: Forest Lookouts lists a SCFC lookout at Oakway, Oconee County. No source we read describes the Oakway tower itself; the story gives statewide SCFC context only.

facts.status_note: No source we read says whether the Oakway tower stands today.

evidence.supports: Oakway listed as a SCFC lookout in Oconee County
evidence.quote: OAKWAY Oconee County South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: Most tower sites 10 acres, the tower and a year-round dwelling (statewide)
evidence.quote: Most tower sites consisted of 10 acres of land, the tower, and a year-round dwelling for the operator.

evidence.supports: Sites let operators grow vegetables and feed domestic livestock (statewide)
evidence.quote: The size of the property allowed tower operators to grow their own vegetables and feed for their domestic livestock.

evidence.supports: Women operators from the 1960s, husbands often firefighters (statewide)
evidence.quote: From the 1960s on, most South Carolina tower operators were women; frequently their husbands were employed as firefighters.

evidence.supports: Post passed from parent to child (statewide)
evidence.quote: In many cases, the tower became a family tradition, with adult children succeeding their parents as tower operators.
The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: Towers phased out in early 1990s; 30 still stand (statewide, undated article)
evidence.quote: South Carolina phased out its towers in the early 1990s. Today, only 30 of them remain standing.

evidence.supports: Some of the surviving towers are used for radio equipment (statewide)
evidence.quote: fire lookout towers are used here and there around the state for radio antennas and other communication equipment

sources.title: Looking out for last fire towers

notes_for_editor: The only Oakway-specific source is the Forest Lookouts page, which gives name, county and agency. Two web searches found no record of an Oakway tower. A Long Mountain lookout in Oconee County appeared in a search snippet only, unconfirmed as the same site. The Post and Courier article is undated in the copy read.
